target.title: feat(android): record and send voice notes from the chat composer
target.body:
Related: #100709 (iOS counterpart: #100946)

## What Problem This Solves

Android users have no way to send a quick, fire-and-forget voice message to their agent from the chat composer. Voice turns and Talk mode are live, synchronous interactions; neither covers "record 30 seconds now, get an answer whenever it's ready." Channels such as Telegram and WhatsApp already accept voice notes and transcribe them through media understanding — only the first-party app lacked a way to produce one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds tap-to-record voice notes to both Android chat composers (main chat screen and chat sheet), reusing the existing `chat.send` attachment path end to end: a new `VoiceNoteRecorderController` state machine (Idle → Recording → Preparing, sealed states) drives a `MediaRecorder`-backed AAC/m4a mono engine (44.1 kHz, 32 kbps) with a named 3-minute cap wired through `setMaxDuration` so the platform cap and the Done button share one finish path. The finished note is staged as a regular pending attachment (`audio/mp4`, named byte bound) and sent with the normal send button. Two contract details worth calling out: the MPEG-4 container's `ftyp` major brand is normalized to `M4A ` because the gateway sniffs attachment bytes with `file-type`, which classifies Android's default `mp42` brand as `video/mp4` and would route the note to video understanding instead of audio transcription; and recording is mutually exclusive with `MicCaptureManager` voice capture (which has no mic arbiter) — the record button is disabled while capture is active, starting capture or Talk is refused while recording, and the controller owns temp-file cleanup through the staging handoff so a cancelled composition cannot leave a recording in the cache. `RECORD_AUDIO` permission is requested lazily on first use. No server changes: gateway `chat.send` already accepts non-image attachments and the reply pipeline transcribes audio via media understanding. Non-goals per the tracking issue: playback of sent notes, waveform visualization, slide-to-cancel, and offline queueing of attachments (attachments stay online-only per the outbox contract).

## User Impact

Android users can tap the mic button next to the attachment control in either composer, record up to 3 minutes with a live timer, cancel or finish, see the note as a "Voice note · m:ss" chip (optionally alongside text), and send it. Sent bubbles render a voice-note row with duration, preserved across the optimistic-echo → history reconciliation. If the gateway is offline, the existing attachments-online-only refusal applies unchanged.

## Evidence

- Full unit run on the rebased branch: 946 tests, with the only 2 failures being pre-existing `GatewayBootstrapAuthTest` coroutine-timeout flakes under heavy machine load — both pass in isolation (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 10s rerun) and that surface is untouched by this diff.
- Focused suites: `VoiceNoteRecorderControllerTest` (12 tests: lifecycle, elapsed clock, duration cap via the max-duration callback, oversize rejection, M4A brand normalization, mic mutual exclusion, permission denial, cancel/failure cleanup including cancel-during-Preparing), `ChatVoiceNoteAttachmentTest` (outgoing payload + local-echo duration), `ChatMessageContentParsingTest`, `ChatControllerMessageIdentityTest` (duration preservation across reconciliation) — all green.
- `:app:ktlintMainSourceSetCheck` and `:app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck` green; `pnpm android:assemble` (Play debug) BUILD SUCCESSFUL with `uses-permission: android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO` in the APK; `pnpm native:i18n:sync` regenerated the catalog.
- Live mic capture is manual-proof by nature; the recorder engine sits behind a fake-driven seam and the assembled APK was inspected source-blind.
